premises.text: Customer service is bad across everyday venues; rating interactions publicly can improve it
An iPhone/HTML5 app rates individual employees with thumbs, comments, social share, and optional response requests in ~30 seconds
premises.evidence_span: in 30 seconds or less, you just provided not only that employee, but also their manager with information

premises.text: Consumers consult employee ratings before choosing a salesperson or service provider
premises.evidence_span: instead of walking in and meeting the first person who walks in the door, maybe you should go on Tello in advance

premises.text: Businesses receive an aggregated dashboard for benchmarks, employee performance, and customer-response inbox
premises.evidence_span: they can compare themselves against other businesses on customer service

premises.text: Partners such as airlines, hotels, and retailers promote Tello via buttons and POS signs; apps integrate with location check-ins
premises.evidence_span: have either buttons they wear or signs at the point of sale that say, hey, let me know how I'm doing on service

premises.text: A large indexed set of businesses can be rated through the system
premises.evidence_span: We have over 14 million businesses, and you can go in and rate them

value.text: Customer service improves when interactions are rated on phones
value.evidence_span: raising the bar on customer service

secondary_value.text: Managers see which employees excel or need help
secondary_value.evidence_span: these are ones who are doing a great job. Maybe they need a promotion

causal_links.evidence_span: by shining a bright light on it, customer service gets better
at a glance see what's going on with their business

notes: 14M businesses coded as coverage condition for the rating theory, not as traction metric alone. Investor list excluded.
